extracted.intended_audience: CNN readers / general public interested in media, comedy, and social justice debates
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and considerations for judging whether a comedian's remarks (on stage or off) are acceptable, hateful, or deserving of sanction; focuses on context, consistency, and societal reactions to jokes about race, sex, sexual orientation, and violence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish performance bit vs non-performance outburst
rubrics_metrics.description: "Richards' N-word blowup wasn't a part of his stand-up act; it wasn't a bit; it wasn't a routine; he lashed out at a patron. Is there a difference? You bet."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether remarks occurred as part of a planned routine or as a private/unscripted outburst; the author treats on-stage bits differently from spontaneous lash-outs when judging consequences and intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context and medium matter (stage, workplace, private)
rubrics_metrics.description: The society will let comedians say things on stage that if someone else said them in the workplace, we would be filing lawsuits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the forum (stage, radio, morning show, workplace, private voicemail) because different settings carry different expectations and potential sanctions (e.g., workplace rules, public fines, private forgiveness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre/role expectations (shock jock vs mainstream host)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our society will have a different standard for a shock jock then we would for a traditional morning show host. Our society will let comedians say things on stage that if someone else said them in the workplace, we would be filing lawsuits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take into account the performer's established genre or role (shock jock, comedian, morning-show host) — audiences and institutions may tolerate different speech from entertainers known for transgression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of societal standards (avoid double standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: So society says it's bad, but then for some it's fine -- so what's the mixed message we're sending?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether reactions are consistent across similar cases; identify hypocrisy where some offenders are excused due to status, cast, or perceived community 'friendship.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider speaker's relationship to targeted group
rubrics_metrics.description: He's a friend of the gay community... Lampanelli used the F-word with impunity while thanking her gay and lesbian fans... He's a friend of the gay community and has donated money to gay causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for whether the performer is perceived as an ally, has donated or shown support to the targeted community, or is a member of that community — these factors affect how statements are judged by some.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severity and nature of content (graphic, violent, hateful)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tracy Morgan's graphic and violent anti-gay 'rant'... I cited examples of jokes about the murder of O.J. Simpson's ex-wife and her friend; a comedian joking he wished he showed up at home and his wife was dead; a ton of jokes about beating kids...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how graphic, violent, or hateful the content is — more extreme or violent depictions and explicit bigotry weigh more heavily in condemnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider societal harms and ongoing epidemics
rubrics_metrics.description: To a socially conscious person, that's an abomination when you look at the HIV/AIDS rates in America... Child abuse is a major problem in America. But don't let me pull out the video clips of comedians... talking about beating a kid...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor in whether jokes target ongoing social crises or vulnerable groups where humor may exacerbate harm or trivialize real suffering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern versus isolated incident
rubrics_metrics.description: He made these comments in private, was on his son's answering machine, wasn't in the workplace, and it didn't rise to the level of him losing his show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the remarks are part of a recurring pattern of behavior or a one-time event; repeat offenses merit different responses than isolated slips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apology and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: I got wind of the issue when I read Morgan's apology for what he had to say.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take into account whether the comedian apologized, sought to make amends, or showed remorse — apologies can influence public judgment and consequences, though they don't erase harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience behavior and private hypocrisy (we laugh but condemn)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you ever laughed at vile, nasty, offensive comics who told sexist, racist and homophobic jokes? The response? A resounding yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that audiences often enjoy or laugh at offensive material even while publicly condemning it; this discrepancy should be part of evaluating both comedians and societal responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power dynamics and who is being punched at
rubrics_metrics.description: When groups that have been oppressed begin to make sweeping pronouncements about what can or cannot be said, there are going to be the contradictions that have to be confronted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether jokes punch up at powerful institutions or down at marginalized groups; power relations influence whether humor is perceived as acceptable or damaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Celebrity status and marketability influence tolerance
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, all of these come from popular comedians who are loved and adored by millions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how fame and popularity insulate performers from criticism or consequence; beloved entertainers may receive more leeway despite offensive material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different standards for similar slurs depending on context and cast
rubrics_metrics.description: A lot of folks were offended when people who were not black used the N-word in 'The Hangover II.' But if that was a movie with a predominantly black cast? Nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that acceptability of slurs can be judged differently depending on who uses them, the cast/performer demographics, and the cultural context of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions should be proportional and situational
rubrics_metrics.description: When Kobe Bryant directed the F-word at a referee and he was caught on camera, there was a huge uproar. He was hit with a $100,000 fine... I was on CNN and was asked if he should lose his A&E show. I said, not at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine appropriate consequences (fines, firing, censure) based on context: public impact, role, pattern, and whether comments were on-duty, off-duty, private, or part of a performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage deeper societal introspection rather than surface rebukes
rubrics_metrics.description: But if we leave it there, and do not become more introspective as a society and confront our own contradictions on race, sex, homophobia and violence, we will have allowed the moment to go to waste and failed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor sustained conversation and self-examination about accepted norms and contradictions in responses to offensive humor instead of brief moralizing or performative outrage.
